items.title: Paul Barbarin Interview, 1957-03-27
items.q: And the same evening I got the drums, John Perdonce heard about it... And that was my first engagement.

ctx.x: Oh, by the way, is this... We talked to Mr. Glenny the other day and he said there was an old bass player. The first one he heard used to play with you. It was the first one that began picking. Perdonce? John Perdonce? John Perdonce? It might have been John Perdonce. Do you remember... By your time they were all picking a good deal, I guess. Yeah, everybody was picking. Yeah, everybody was picking that time. My time. So you started on drums just in the kitchen, you say. Then you didn't have a drum to start on.

No, so I went to work at St. Charles Hotel. I was running the freight elevator there. And I get paid every two weeks. So my mother knew I wanted to set a drum, so she said, well, let's put the money aside. So at one time I had enough to make a down payment. So we go over to Glenwall, where my father dealt that to me. And the sign-ups got me a set of drums. And the same evening I got the drums, John Perdonce heard about it. He didn't have a drum to play. He played somebody's fixin' run for us, some hardman or…
What was Longhead Bob's last name?
